text: Embedded APK blobs grow the repo ~2.4 MB per release — decide a policy

Decided: keep committing the APK. Rejecting rather than leaving open, so the
question is answered in the tracker instead of being re-asked.

Measured at decision time (2026-09-01, at v1.12.0 plus 5 commits):

  .git total              53 MB
  APK blobs in history    19, 41.1 MiB of it
  growth per release      ~2.2 MiB
  releases so far         21
  web_dist asset blobs    32, 6.5 MiB (same pattern, not worth acting on)

Why not the alternatives:

- git LFS keeps the clone-and-build property but adds a dependency for everyone
  who clones, does nothing about the 41 MiB already in history, and carries its
  own quota on GitHub.
- Untracking the APK is the only option that shrinks anything, but it costs the
  property that a fresh clone builds a complete wheel with no Android toolchain
  — a real case for someone self-hosting from source — and would mean rewriting
  the single-artifact section of the README.

At ~2.2 MiB per release the repo reaches GitHub's first complaint after several
hundred more releases. The fixes cost more than the problem does. Revisit only
if .git passes ~250 MB.
